I have resolved the issue where deferred fields on nested prefetches following back to a parent object were overwritten by the parent instance's deferred fields state.

### Cause
When evaluating `get_prefetch_queryset` on relational descriptors (`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`, `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`, and `ReverseManyToOneDescriptor`), Django sets the reverse relationship cache on each retrieved related object (`rel_obj`) pointing back to the parent `instance`. When nested prefetches were specified on the related object back to the parent (such as `Prefetch("user", queryset=User.objects.only(...))`), the nested prefetch was evaluated first during iteration of the related queryset. However, right after that, `get_prefetch_queryset` unconditionally assigned `instance` (the top-level parent object with its own deferred fields set) to `rel_obj`, overwriting the newly prefetched instance.

### Solution
In [`django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-9l9syp50/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L145-L150):
Before setting the reverse relation cache on `rel_obj` inside `get_prefetch_queryset`, check whether the relation on `rel_obj` is already cached (`is_cached(rel_obj)`). If it was already cached (for instance, by an inner prefetch queryset), preserve the existing cached instance instead of overwriting it with the outer parent instance.
The issue has been resolved and verified with tests. All prefetch and defer test suites pass cleanly.
